name: Religious Studies
specTitle: GCSE Religious Studies A (Short Course) — Christianity and Islam
confidenceNote: Board, code and religions confirmed. Open question: the Year 11 RS scheme of work covers the death penalty, abortion and euthanasia, which are not on the 8061 short course. Almost certainly non-examined Year 11 RS taught after the exam — worth one email to the school to be sure.

papers.name: Religious Studies A (Short Course)
papers.notes: 96 marks plus 6 for spelling, punctuation and grammar. Section A: the two religions. Section B: both themes. Linear — one paper at the end of the course.

examNotes: One paper, 1h45, the whole qualification. Sat in Year 10 — summer 2027.
Section A is beliefs and teachings only. Practices are NOT on the short course.
Question structure per topic: 1 mark, 2 marks, 4 marks, 5 marks, then a 12-mark evaluation. The 12-marker is where the grade is won.
The 12-mark evaluation needs arguments for, arguments against, reference to religious teaching, and a justified conclusion. Six marks of the paper are for SPaG — write in full, accurate sentences.
Learn short scriptural quotations for both religions. A named source of authority lifts an answer out of the middle band.

units.title: The study of religions: beliefs and teachings

points.statement: The nature of God: God as omnipotent, loving and just, and the problem of evil and suffering
detail: Omnipotent — all-powerful; loving — God cares for creation; just — God judges fairly
The problem of evil: if God is all-powerful and all-loving, why does suffering exist?
Christian responses include free will, suffering as a test, and Jesus sharing in human suffering

points.statement: The oneness of God and the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
detail: One God in three persons — not three Gods
Basis in the baptism of Jesus and the Nicene Creed

points.statement: Different Christian beliefs about creation, including the role of the Word and the Spirit
detail: Genesis 1 — God creates through the Word
John 1:1-3 identifies the Word with Christ

points.statement: Different Christian beliefs about the afterlife and their importance, including resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell
Beliefs and teachings about the incarnation and Jesus as the Son of God
Beliefs and teachings about the crucifixion, resurrection and ascension
Beliefs and teachings about sin, including original sin
Beliefs and teachings about the means of salvation, including law, grace and Spirit
The role of Christ in salvation, including the idea of atonement
The six articles of faith in Sunni Islam and the five roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam, including key similarities and differences
detail: Sunni six articles: Tawhid, angels, holy books, prophets, Day of Judgement, predestination
Shi'a five roots: Tawhid, divine justice (Adalat), prophethood, imamate, resurrection

points.statement: Tawhid: the Oneness of God, with reference to the Qur'an
detail: Surah 112 — God is one, eternal, not begotten
Shirk (associating partners with God) is the gravest sin

points.statement: The nature of God, including omnipotence, beneficence, mercy, fairness and justice
detail: Adalat — divine justice, particularly emphasised in Shi'a Islam

points.statement: Angels, their nature and role, including Jibril and Mika'il
Predestination and human freedom, and its relationship to the Day of Judgement
Akhirah: life after death, human responsibility and accountability, resurrection, heaven and hell
Risalah (prophethood), including the role and importance of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad
The holy books: Qur'an, Tawrat, Zabur, Injil and Sahifah, their nature, authority and importance
detail: The Qur'an is the final and unaltered revelation, given to Muhammad through the angel Jibril

points.statement: The imamate in Shi'a Islam: its role and significance

topics.title: Theme A: Sex, marriage and divorce

points.statement: Human sexuality, including heterosexual and same-sex relationships
Sexual relationships before and outside of marriage
Contraception and family planning
The nature and purpose of marriage
Same-sex marriage and cohabitation
Divorce, including reasons for divorce and remarrying
Ethical arguments related to divorce, including those based on the sanctity of marriage vows and compassion

topics.title: Theme A: Families and gender equality

points.statement: The nature of families, including the role of parents and children, and extended and nuclear families
The purpose of families, including procreation, stability, the protection of children, and educating children in a faith
Contemporary family issues, including same-sex parents and polygamy
The roles of men and women
Gender equality
Gender prejudice and discrimination, including examples

topics.title: Theme B: Religion, violence, terrorism and war

points.statement: The meaning and significance of peace, justice, forgiveness and reconciliation
Violence, including violent protest
Terrorism
Reasons for war, including greed, self-defence and retaliation
The just war theory, including the criteria for a just war
detail: Just cause, proper authority, right intention, last resort, proportionality, reasonable chance of success

points.statement: Holy war
detail: In Islam, greater and lesser jihad — the greater jihad is the personal struggle to live faithfully

points.statement: Pacifism

topics.title: Theme B: Religion and belief in 21st century conflict

points.statement: Religion and belief as a cause of war and violence in the contemporary world
Nuclear weapons, including nuclear deterrence
The use of weapons of mass destruction
Religion and peace-making in the contemporary world, including the work of individuals influenced by religious teaching
Religious responses to the victims of war, including the work of one present-day religious organisation
detail: Learn one named organisation in detail — Christian Aid, Islamic Relief, Muslim Aid or CAFOD
